name: Gazetteer Named Place Source Nodes
description: The PURE half of the GeoNames gazetteer lane: it decodes a gazetteer dump into $GNP records and does nothing else. capabilities [], browser + wasmedge, request-scoped, no state between invocations. Every byte it decodes was fetched by com.digitalarsenal.hostcap.http-request and every record it emits is persisted by com.digitalarsenal.hostcap.storage-ingest; the scheduling, chunking and resume decisions live in the sibling com.digitalarsenal.data-source.geonames-ingest, exactly as cell-tower-source and cell-tower-ingest are split. The seed edition ships as a ZIP and there is no host unzip capability (and none may be added), so miniz 3.1.2 is vendored under vendor/miniz-3.1.2 (MIT, SHA-256 pinned and re-verified on every build) and the archive's central directory is walked in-guest - the same vendored copy data-source/cell-tower-source already uses for the national bulk archives. $GNP requires RESOLVED admin and country NAMES beside the codes, which is why the division/country files are decoded into a lookup frame and joined at parse time rather than left to a consumer.

sequentialJustification.detail: All four methods are single-pass transforms over the frames the flow hands them: inflate one archive member, fold three text files into a lookup table, decode tab-separated rows into records, decode tombstone rows into a list. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest, so it compiles single-thread rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Turns the fetched body into plain text. container="zip" walks the archive's CENTRAL DIRECTORY (never the local header, which carries zeroes under a data descriptor and would inflate to an empty gazetteer) and inflates the named member, or the first member when none is named; container="plain" passes the body through, which is what the daily modifications/deletes and the three lookup files need. A non-2xx status and a short inflate are both REFUSED rather than decoded to a partial answer: an empty edition and a failed fetch must never be the same observation. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

methods.description: $GNP carries a RESOLVED NAME beside every administrative and country code, 'so a consumer need not hold the division tables to render a place'. The gazetteer publishes those names in three separate plain-text files, so they are folded here into one lookup frame that parse_places joins against. A file the flow did not fetch simply contributes nothing and the affected places carry their codes with the name left UNSET - a missing name is recoverable, a wrong one is not. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. methods.description: Decodes the 19-column geoname row shape into $GNP. The SEED and the DAILY DELTA use this one decoder because modifications-YYYY-MM-DD.txt is a file of FULL geoname rows (verified live 2026-08-15), so a modification is an upsert of exactly the record the seed would have produced and there is no second record shape to keep in step. A job that cannot state DATASET_ID, DATASET_EPOCH and LICENSE is REFUSED, never defaulted: a place published under a guessed epoch is comparable to the wrong bytes. A position outside the WGS 84 domain is DROPPED and counted, never clamped, because a clamped place is a place in the wrong location. Columns the gazetteer leaves empty are left UNSET rather than zeroed, which is what keeps 'no elevation published' distinguishable from 'an elevation of zero'. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

methods.description: Decodes deletes-YYYY-MM-DD.txt (three tab-separated columns, verified live 2026-08-15) into a tombstone list, carrying each removal REASON verbatim because 'duplicate' and 'not a real place' are different facts about the same id. A row whose first column is not a decimal id is skipped and counted - the gazetteer serves an HTML 404 body for a day it no longer retains, and decoding that into tombstones is the exact failure this guard exists for. THIS EMITS A LIST, NOT A DELETION: no host capability removes a stored row (storage-ingest offers ingest only; flatsql-query is read-only) and inventing one would be a new host capability this lane may not add, so the list leaves the flow on its own port and the durable delete lane is recorded as a gap rather than faked. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed.
